sanskrit: athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ nārācānāṃ tribhiḥ śataiḥ vivyādha bharataśreṣṭha śrutakarmā mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then, O best of the Bhāratas, when his bow had been cut away, the illustrious Śrutakarman pierced him with three hundred iron-shafted arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena bhṛśaṃ tīkṣṇena satvaraḥ jahāra saśirastrāṇaṃ śiras tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft, exceedingly sharp, the swift warrior swept off the head of that great-souled one, helmet and all.

sanskrit: tacchiro nyapatad bhūmau sumahac citravarmaṇaḥ yadṛcchayā yathā candraś cyutaḥ svargān mahītale
english: That mighty head of Citravarman fell upon the earth, as the moon, fallen by some chance from heaven, might drop to the ground.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā abhisāraṃ ca māriṣa abhyadravanta vegena citrasenasya sainikāḥ
english: Seeing their king slain and Abhisāra fallen too, O honored one, the soldiers of Citrasena rushed forward with fury.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho maheṣvāsas tat sainyaṃ prādravac charaiḥ antakāle yathā kruddhaḥ sarvabhūtāni pretarāṭ drāvayann iṣubhis tūrṇaṃ śrutakarmā vyarocata
english: Then that wrathful mighty bowman scattered the host with his arrows; as the lord of the dead in his fury drives all creatures before him at the hour of doom, so Śrutakarman, swiftly routing them with his shafts, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: prativindhyas tataś citraṃ bhittvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ sārathiṃ tribhir ānarcchad dhvajam ekeṣuṇā tataḥ
english: Then Prativindhya, having pierced Citra with five swift arrows, struck his charioteer with three, and his banner thereafter with a single shaft.

sanskrit: taṃ citro navabhir bhallair bāhvor urasi cārdayat svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilādhautaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ
english: Citra in turn tormented him in the arms and breast with nine broad-headed shafts, gold-feathered, whetted on stone, and winged with the plumes of heron and peacock.

sanskrit: prativindhyo dhanus tasya chittvā bhārata sāyakaiḥ pañcabhir niśitair bāṇair athainaṃ saṃprajaghnivān
english: Prativindhya, O Bhārata, cut his bow asunder with arrows, and then smote him fiercely with five sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ mahārāja hemadaṇḍāṃ durāsadām prāhiṇot tava putrāya ghorām agniśikhām iva
english: Then, O great king, he hurled at your son a lance with a golden shaft, hard to withstand, terrible as a tongue of flame.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śaktim ulkām ivāmbarāt dvidhā ciccheda samare prativindhyo hasann iva
english: As that lance came rushing down like a meteor from the sky, Prativindhya, as if smiling, cut it in twain upon the field.

sanskrit: sā papāta tadā chinnā prativindhyaśaraiḥ śitaiḥ yugānte sarvabhūtāni trāsayantī yathāśaniḥ
english: Cleft by Prativindhya's keen arrows, it fell to earth, like a thunderbolt at the end of an age that strikes terror into all beings.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ tāṃ prahatāṃ dṛṣṭvā citro gṛhya mahāgadām prativindhyāya cikṣepa rukmajālavibhūṣitām
english: Seeing his lance struck down, Citra seized a great mace, adorned with a network of gold, and flung it at Prativindhya.

sanskrit: sā jaghāna hayāṃs tasya sārathiṃ ca mahāraṇe rathaṃ pramṛdya vegena dharaṇīm anvapadyata
english: In that great battle it slew his horses and his charioteer, and crushing the chariot with its force, sank into the earth.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu rathād āplutya bhārata śaktiṃ cikṣepa citrāya svarṇaghaṇṭām alaṃkṛtām
english: At that very moment, O Bhārata, leaping down from his chariot, he hurled at Citra a lance bedecked with bells of gold.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ jagrāha citro rājan mahāmanāḥ tatas tām eva cikṣepa prativindhyāya bhārata
english: As it flew toward him, the high-souled Citra caught it, O king, and hurled that same lance back at Prativindhya, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: samāsādya raṇe śūraṃ prativindhyaṃ mahāprabhā nirbhidya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ nipapāta mahītale patitābhāsayac caiva taṃ deśam aśanir yathā
english: Reaching the hero Prativindhya in battle, that lance of great brilliance pierced his right arm and fell to the ground; and where it fell it lit up that place like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: prativindhyas tato rājaṃs tomaraṃ hemabhūṣitam preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaś citrasya vadhakāmyayā
english: Then, O king, Prativindhya in his wrath sent forth a gold-decked iron dart, desiring the death of Citra.

sanskrit: sa tasya devāvaraṇaṃ bhittvā hṛdayam eva ca jagāma dharaṇīṃ tūrṇaṃ mahoraga ivāśayam
english: Piercing the bright armor that guarded him, and his very heart as well, it passed swiftly into the earth, like a great serpent gliding into its hole.

sanskrit: sa papāta tadā rājaṃs tomareṇa samāhataḥ prasārya vipulau bāhū pīnau parighasaṃnibhau
english: Smitten by that dart, he fell then, O king, stretching out his two broad arms, thick and round as iron bludgeons.

sanskrit: citraṃ saṃprekṣya nihataṃ tāvakā raṇaśobhinaḥ abhyadravanta vegena prativindhyaṃ samantataḥ
english: Seeing Citra slain, your warriors, the ornaments of battle, rushed with fury upon Prativindhya from every side.

sanskrit: sṛjanto vividhān bāṇāñ śataghnīś ca sakiṅkiṇīḥ ta enaṃ chādayām āsuḥ sūryam abhragaṇā iva
english: Loosing arrows of many kinds and bell-hung śataghnīs, they covered him over as banks of cloud cover the sun.

sanskrit: tān apāsya mahābāhuḥ śarajālena saṃyuge vyadrāvayat tava camūṃ vajrahasta ivāsurīm
english: But the mighty-armed one swept them aside with his web of arrows in the fray, and routed your host as the wielder of the thunderbolt routs the army of the Asuras.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavair nṛpa viprakīryanta sahasā vātanunnā ghanā iva
english: Slaughtered in the battle by the Pāṇḍavas, O king, your men were scattered all at once like clouds driven before the wind.

sanskrit: vipradrute bale tasmin vadhyamāne samantataḥ drauṇir eko 'bhyayāt tūrṇaṃ bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: When that army had fled and was being slain on every side, the son of Droṇa, alone, swiftly bore down upon the mighty Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāgamo ghoro babhūva sahasā tayoḥ yathā devāsure yuddhe vṛtravāsavayor abhūt
english: Then there arose of a sudden a fearful encounter between the two, such as was the clash of Vṛtra and Vāsava in the war of the gods and the Asuras.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenaṃ tato drauṇī rājan vivyādha patriṇā tvarayā parayā yukto darśayann astralāghavam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, O king, the son of Droṇa pierced Bhīmasena with a winged shaft, moving with utmost speed and displaying the lightness of his hand with weapons.

sanskrit: athainaṃ punar ājaghne navatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sarvamarmāṇi saṃprekṣya marmajño laghuhastavat
english: Then again he struck him with ninety sharpened arrows, marking all his vital points—knowing the vitals well, and nimble of hand.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaḥ samākīrṇo drauṇinā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rarāja samare rājan raśmivān iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Bhīmasena, thickly studded by the son of Droṇa with keen arrows, shone in the battle, O king, like the radiant sun crowned with its beams.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa suprayuktena pāṇḍavaḥ droṇaputram avacchādya siṃhanādam amuñcata
english: Then with a thousand well-aimed arrows the son of Pāṇḍu veiled the son of Droṇa, and let loose a lion's roar.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ śarāṃs tato drauṇiḥ saṃvārya yudhi pāṇḍavam lalāṭe 'bhyahanad rājan nārācena smayann iva
english: Then the son of Droṇa, warding off arrows with arrows in the fight, struck the son of Pāṇḍu upon the brow with an iron shaft, O king, as if in mockery.

sanskrit: lalāṭasthaṃ tato bāṇaṃ dhārayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ yathā śṛṅgaṃ vane dṛptaḥ khaḍgo dhārayate nṛpa
english: The son of Pāṇḍu bore that arrow lodged in his forehead, O king, as a proud rhinoceros of the forest bears its horn.

sanskrit: tato drauṇiṃ raṇe bhīmo yatamānaṃ parākramī tribhir vivyādha nārācair lalāṭe vismayann iva
english: Then the valiant Bhīma, as the son of Droṇa pressed on in battle, pierced him in the brow with three iron shafts, as if to amaze him.

sanskrit: lalāṭasthais tato bāṇair brāhmaṇaḥ sa vyarocata prāvṛṣīva yathā siktas triśṛṅgaḥ parvatottamaḥ
english: With those arrows fixed upon his forehead the Brāhmaṇa shone forth, like some lofty three-peaked mountain drenched in the rains.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatair drauṇim ardayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ na cainaṃ kampayām āsa mātariśveva parvatam
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu tormented the son of Droṇa with hundreds of arrows, yet shook him not, as the wind cannot shake a mountain.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe drauṇiḥ śaraśataiḥ śitaiḥ nākampayata saṃhṛṣṭo vāryogha iva parvatam
english: In like manner the son of Droṇa, exultant, could not shake the son of Pāṇḍu in the fight with hundreds of keen arrows, as a flood cannot shake a mountain.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ śarair ghoraiś chādayānau mahārathau rathacaryāgatau śūrau śuśubhāte raṇotkaṭau
english: Those two great car-warriors, veiling each other with terrible arrows, both heroes skilled in the maneuvers of the chariot, shone resplendent, fierce in the joy of battle.

sanskrit: ādityāv iva saṃdīptau lokakṣayakarāv ubhau svaraśmibhir ivānyonyaṃ tāpayantau śarottamaiḥ
english: Both blazing like two suns that work the world's destruction, they scorched each other with their finest shafts as suns scorch with their own rays.

sanskrit: kṛtapratikṛte yatnaṃ kurvāṇau ca mahāraṇe kṛtapratikṛte yatnaṃ cakrāte tāv abhītavat
english: In that great battle they strove, each to answer the other's stroke with a stroke; fearlessly the two contended, blow for matching blow.

sanskrit: vyāghrāv iva ca saṃgrāme ceratus tau mahārathau śaradaṃṣṭrau durādharṣau cāpavyāttau bhayānakau
english: Like two tigers the two mighty car-warriors ranged the field, their arrows for fangs, unassailable, their bows agape like jaws, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: abhūtāṃ tāv adṛśyau ca śarajālaiḥ samantataḥ meghajālair iva cchannau gagane candrabhāskarau
english: The two became invisible, hidden on every side by their webs of arrows, like the moon and the sun veiled by masses of cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: prakāśau ca muhūrtena tatraivāstām ariṃdamau vimuktau meghajālena śaśisūryau yathā divi
english: And in a moment those subduers of foes shone forth again upon that field, like the moon and the sun in the heavens freed from the masses of cloud.

sanskrit: apasavyaṃ tataś cakre drauṇis tatra vṛkodaram kirañ śaraśatair ugrair dhārābhir iva parvatam
english: Then the son of Droṇa wheeled to the left around Vṛkodara there, drenching him with hundreds of fierce arrows as rain-streams drench a mountain.

sanskrit: na tu tan mamṛṣe bhīmaḥ śatror vijayalakṣaṇam praticakre ca taṃ rājan pāṇḍavo 'py apasavyataḥ
english: But Bhīma could not brook that mark of his foe's mastery, and the son of Pāṇḍu, O king, wheeled in answer about him likewise to the left.

sanskrit: maṇḍalānāṃ vibhāgeṣu gatapratyāgateṣu ca babhūva tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ tayos tatra mahāmṛdhe
english: Through the divisions of their circling courses, in their advances and returns, a tumultuous combat arose between the two upon that great field.

sanskrit: caritvā vividhān mārgān maṇḍalaṃ sthānam eva ca śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Coursing through their various movements—the circle and the steady stand—they smote each other with arrows loosed from bows drawn to the full.

sanskrit: anyonyasya vadhe yatnaṃ cakratus tau mahārathau īṣatur virathaṃ caiva kartum anyonyam āhave
english: The two great car-warriors each strove to slay the other, and each sought in the encounter to strip the other of his chariot.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir mahāstrāṇi prāduścakre mahārathaḥ tāny astrair eva samare pratijaghne 'sya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa, that mighty car-warrior, brought forth his great celestial weapons; and in the battle the son of Pāṇḍu beat them back with weapons of his own.

sanskrit: tato ghoraṃ mahārāja astrayuddham avartata grahayuddhaṃ yathā ghoraṃ prajāsaṃharaṇe abhūt
english: Then, O great king, a fearful battle of celestial weapons raged on, terrible as the war of the planets at the destruction of all created beings.

sanskrit: te bāṇāḥ samasajjanta kṣiptās tābhyāṃ tu bhārata dyotayanto diśaḥ sarvās tac ca sainyaṃ samantataḥ
english: Those arrows, hurled by the two, clashed together, O Bhārata, lighting up all the quarters and that army round about.

sanskrit: bāṇasaṃghāvṛtaṃ ghoram ākāśaṃ samapadyata uklāpātakṛtaṃ yadvat prajānāṃ saṃkṣaye nṛpa
english: The sky grew terrible, overspread by the throngs of arrows, as though strewn with falling meteors at the destruction of created beings, O king.

sanskrit: bāṇābhighātāt saṃjajñe tatra bhārata pāvakaḥ savisphuliṅgo dīptārciḥ so 'dahad vāhinīdvayam
english: From the clash of arrows a fire was born there, O Bhārata, scattering sparks and blazing with flame, and it scorched both the contending hosts.

sanskrit: tatra siddhā mahārāja saṃpatanto 'bruvan vacaḥ ati yuddhāni sarvāṇi yuddham etat tato 'dhikam
english: Then the Siddhas, O great king, hovering above, spoke these words: "This battle surpasses all battles whatsoever; greater is it than all the rest.

sanskrit: sarvayuddhāni caitasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm naitādṛśaṃ punar yuddhaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
english: All other battles are not worth a sixteenth part of this; no such combat has ever been, nor shall ever be again.

sanskrit: aho jñānena saṃyuktāv ubhau cograparākramau aho bhīme balaṃ bhīmam etayoś ca kṛtāstratā
english: Ah, how endowed with knowledge are these two, and how fierce in valor! Ah, the dreadful strength of Bhīma, and the weapon-skill of both!

sanskrit: aho vīryasya sāratvam aho sauṣṭhavam etayoḥ sthitāv etau hi samare kālāntakayamopamau
english: Ah, the very pith of prowess, ah, the perfect mastery of these two! There they stand in the battle, like Yama the Ender at the close of time.

sanskrit: rudrau dvāv iva saṃbhūtau yathā dvāv iva bhāskarau yamau vā puruṣavyāghrau ghorarūpāv imau raṇe
english: Like two Rudras come to being, like two suns, or like the twin Aśvins—so are these tigers among men, terrible of form upon the field."

sanskrit: śrūyante sma tadā vācaḥ siddhānāṃ vai muhur muhuḥ siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe sametānāṃ divaukasām adbhutaṃ cāpy acintyaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā karma tayor mṛdhe
english: Such words of the Siddhas were heard then again and again, and a lion's roar arose from the assembled dwellers of heaven, beholding the wondrous and unimaginable deeds of the two in that fray.

sanskrit: tau śūrau samare rājan parasparakṛtāgasau parasparam udaikṣetāṃ krodhād udvṛtya cakṣuṣī
english: Those two heroes in the battle, O king, each having wronged the other, glared upon each other, rolling their eyes in wrath.

sanskrit: krodharaktekṣaṇau tau tu krodhāt prasphuritādharau krodhāt saṃdaṣṭadaśanau saṃdaṣṭadaśanacchadau
english: Their eyes red with anger, their lips quivering in anger, in their anger grinding their teeth and biting their lips,

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ chādayantau sma śaravṛṣṭyā mahārathau śarāmbudhārau samare śastravidyutprakāśinau
english: the two great car-warriors veiled each other with a downpour of arrows, raining floods of shafts upon the field, gleaming with the lightning of their weapons.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ dhvajau viddhvā sārathī ca mahārathau anyonyasya hayān viddhvā bibhidāte parasparam
english: Those two great car-warriors, having pierced each other's banner and charioteer, and having pierced each other's horses, wounded one another.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhau mahārāja bāṇau gṛhya mahāhave ubhau cikṣipatus tūrṇam anyonyasya vadhaiṣiṇau
english: Then in their wrath, O great king, in that great battle, both seized arrows and swiftly hurled them, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: tau sāyakau mahārāja dyotamānau camūmukhe ājaghnāte samāsādya vajravegau durāsadau
english: Those two arrows, O great king, gleaming at the head of the host, swift as the thunderbolt and hard to bear, met and struck home.

sanskrit: tau parasparavegāc ca śarābhyāṃ ca bhṛśāhatau nipetatur mahāvīrau svarathopasthayos tadā
english: By the force of their rushing and grievously smitten by those two shafts, the two great heroes then sank down, each upon the floor of his own chariot.

sanskrit: tatas tu sārathir jñātvā droṇaputram acetanam apovāha raṇād rājan sarvakṣatrasya paśyataḥ
english: Then the charioteer, knowing the son of Droṇa to be senseless, bore him away from the battle, O king, while all the warriors looked on.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavaṃ rājan vihvalantaṃ muhur muhuḥ apovāha rathenājau sārathiḥ śatrutāpanam
english: In like manner, O king, the charioteer bore away from the fight upon his car that scorcher of foes, the son of Pāṇḍu, who reeled again and again.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yathā saṃśaptakaiḥ sārdham arjunasyābhavad raṇaḥ anyeṣāṃ ca madīyānāṃ pāṇḍavais tad bravīhi me
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me how the battle of Arjuna went against the Saṃśaptakas, and how it fared for the others of my side against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathāvṛttaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ bruvato mama vīrāṇāṃ śatrubhiḥ sārdhaṃ dehapāpmapraṇāśanam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, as I relate the battle as it befell—the combat of our heroes against their foes, a combat that purges away the body's sins.

sanskrit: pārthaḥ saṃśaptakagaṇaṃ praviśyārṇavasaṃnibham vyakṣobhayad amitraghno mahāvāta ivārṇavam
english: The son of Pṛthā, that slayer of foes, plunging into the host of the Saṃśaptakas which was like an ocean, churned it up as a great wind churns the sea.

sanskrit: śirāṃsy unmathya vīrāṇāṃ śitair bhallair dhanaṃjayaḥ pūrṇacandrābhavaktrāṇi svakṣibhrūdaśanāni ca saṃtastāra kṣitiṃ kṣipraṃ vinālair nalinair iva
english: Striking off with keen broad-headed shafts the heads of the heroes—faces bright as the full moon, with fair eyes, brows, and teeth—Dhanaṃjaya swiftly strewed the earth with them, as with lotuses bereft of their stalks.

sanskrit: suvṛttān āyatān puṣṭāṃś candanāgurubhūṣitān sāyudhān satanutrāṇān pañcāsyoragasaṃnibhān bāhūn kṣurair amitrāṇāṃ vicakartārjuno raṇe
english: The arms of his foes—shapely, long, and full, anointed with sandal and aloe, bearing weapons, clad in armor, like five-hooded serpents—Arjuna severed with his razor-edged shafts in the battle.

sanskrit: dhuryān dhuryatarān sūtān dhvajāṃś cāpāni sāyakān pāṇīn aratnīn asakṛd bhallaiś ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Yoke-horses and the foremost team-horses, charioteers, banners, bows, arrows, hands and forearms—again and again the son of Pāṇḍu cut them away with his broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: dvipān hayān rathāṃś caiva sārohān arjuno raṇe śarair anekasāhasrai rājan ninye yamakṣayam
english: Elephants, horses, and chariots with their riders, Arjuna in the battle, O king, sent with arrows by the many thousands to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: taṃ pravīraṃ pratīyātā nardamānā ivarṣabhāḥ vāśitārtham abhikruddhā huṃkṛtvā cābhidudruvuḥ nighnantam abhijaghnus te śaraiḥ śṛṅgair ivarṣabhāḥ
english: Advancing upon that great hero, bellowing like bulls enraged for the sake of a cow, they rushed at him with roars; and as he smote them, they struck back at him with their arrows, as bulls gore with their horns.

sanskrit: tasya teṣāṃ ca tad yuddham abhaval lomaharṣaṇam trailokyavijaye yādṛg daityānāṃ saha vajriṇā
english: That battle of his with them made the hair stand on end, like the war of the Daityas with the wielder of the thunderbolt for the conquest of the three worlds.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya dviṣatāṃ sarvato 'rjunaḥ iṣubhir bahubhis tūrṇaṃ viddhvā prāṇān rarāsa saḥ
english: Warding off the weapons of his foes on every side with weapons of his own, Arjuna swiftly pierced their very lives with a multitude of shafts, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: chinnatriveṇucakrākṣān hatayodhāśvasārathīn vidhvastāyudhatūṇīrān samunmathitaketanān
english: With their triple bamboo poles, wheels, and axles severed, their warriors, horses, and charioteers slain, their weapons and quivers shattered, their banners struck down,

sanskrit: saṃchinnayoktraraśmīkān vitriveṇūn vikūbarān vidhvastabandhurayugān viśastāyudhamaṇḍalān rathān viśakalīkurvan mahābhrāṇīva mārutaḥ
english: their traces and reins cut through, robbed of their poles and shafts, their seats and yokes broken apart, the array of their weapons hewn down—those chariots he shattered into fragments, as the wind tears great clouds asunder.

sanskrit: vismāpayan prekṣaṇīyaṃ dviṣātāṃ bhayavardhanam mahārathasahasrasya samaṃ karmārjuno 'karot
english: Filling all with wonder, a sight worth beholding and a terror to his foes, Arjuna wrought a deed equal to that of a thousand great car-warriors.

sanskrit: siddhadevarṣisaṃghāś ca cāraṇāś caiva tuṣṭuvuḥ devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi cāpatan keśavārjunayor mūrdhni prāha vāk cāśarīriṇī
english: The hosts of Siddhas, divine sages, and Cāraṇas sang his praises; the kettledrums of the gods resounded, showers of flowers fell upon the heads of Keśava and Arjuna, and a bodiless voice spoke.
